chunks: Hammad narrated from Hariz from Zurara who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): Does a man purify his wealth if one-third of the year has passed? He said: 'No.' I said: Do you offer the first (installment) before midday? He said: 'No.' The Sheikh (peace be upon him) said: And concessions have come from the Infallible Imams (peace be upon them) regarding offering it two months before its due time, and delaying it two months, and it has come three months and four months when there is a need for that.

key_terms.اَلزَّوَالِ: Midday (when the sun passes its zenith)
key_terms.اَلصَّادِقِينَ: The Infallible Imams (specifically referring to Imam al-Sadiq and his predecessors)

ai.seo_question: Can Zakat be paid early or late according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the flexibility in Zakat timing, moving beyond the strict prohibition of paying before the due date to permit concessions of up to four months early or late based on necessity. Al-Tusi highlights the jurisprudential principle of *rukhas* (dispensations) within the Imami school, demonstrating how practical needs allow for deviation from the standard annual cycle. This reflects the broader Shia legal methodology of balancing strict adherence to divine timing with ease for the believer.
